title: Version Instructions and Skills Across Tools
subtitle: Advanced · One repository, two agent clients

scenes.title: Start with a convention you can test
scenes.body: Both approved GCP clients start from the same training checkout.
scenes.code:
After a quantity-validator edit, record:
1. Exact test command
2. Test outcome
3. Files inspected
scenes.narration: Imagine a reviewer opens a training pull request and sees only the words 'tests passed.' Which tests, and on what files? We'll give both agent clients a convention that answers those questions. Whenever the quantity validator changes, the evidence should name the exact test command, the outcome, and the files checked. Those three fields give us a clear pass condition for this exercise.
scenes.focus: Three evidence fields reviewers can check
scenes.action: Choose a convention with observable output.

scenes.title: Put the procedure in a skill
scenes.body: The skill packages a procedure for training PR evidence.
scenes.code:
---
name: training-test-evidence
description: Summarize test evidence for training PRs.
---
Record command, outcome, and inspected files.
scenes.result: A named skill with a concrete description
scenes.narration: Next, open Skill dot M D. The description explains when the procedure is useful: summarizing test evidence for a training pull request. The body says which fields to return and in what format. If you need a reusable evidence template, include it with the skill in a location the client supports. Keep the first version short so you can tell which part helped.
scenes.focus: The description names a specific task
scenes.action: Read the trigger and evidence steps in SKILL.md.

scenes.title: Check the skill on a relevant task
scenes.body: Feed both sessions the same recorded test output.
scenes.code:
Summarize this training PR's validation evidence.
Use the supplied test run and file list.
scenes.result:
Command: python -m unittest discover -s tests -v
Outcome: 4 passed
Scope: validator and zero-boundary test
scenes.narration: Start a fresh session in each client and provide the same recorded run. Ask for the pull request evidence summary. The example returns the command, four passing tests, and the validator and zero-boundary test as the checked scope. Confirm each item against the captured run. If the client shows the skill invocation, note that signal alongside the behavior you observed.

scenes.title: Try an unrelated request
scenes.body: Check that the summary format appears only where useful.
scenes.code:
Explain how order IDs are formatted.
Give the file path that defines the format.
scenes.result: Expected: a concise answer with a source file.
scenes.narration: Try a second prompt: explain how order IDs are formatted, and cite the defining file. The skill's test-evidence output would add clutter here. Look for a simple explanation and a path instead. This gives you a practical two-case test for the skill: one matching request and one unrelated request. Keep both examples when you revise the description.

scenes.title: Confirm the tool boundary
scenes.body: The skill describes the procedure. Effective policy controls execution.
scenes.code:
Convention → what evidence to record
Skill      → how to format the evidence
Policy     → whether the test command can run
scenes.result: The reviewer makes the PR decision with their account.
scenes.narration: Notice that the evidence template includes a test command. A repository file can describe that command and the skill can format its output. The workspace controls whether the client may execute it and whether approval is needed. Read the proposed command and the actual policy. The author can then hand the resulting evidence to an independent reviewer for a decision.
scenes.focus: Command approval is a workspace control
scenes.action: Check permission before any proposed test command.

scenes.title: Review the instructions as code
scenes.body: The pull request records the checked behavior.
scenes.code:
git status --short
git diff -- CLAUDE.md AGENTS.md .claude .opencode
Matching task: all three evidence fields
Unrelated task: cited order-ID explanation
scenes.result: Capture the client versions with both outcomes.
scenes.narration: Review the persistent instruction files and the skill files in the repository diff. Include the matching and unrelated results in the pull request, along with the client versions. Someone reading that evidence should be able to reproduce both outcomes. Then one person can keep the rule aligned across tools while a separate reviewer checks what changed.

scenes.action: Review both instruction files and both skill copies.
